cells.tense: The long build is near its end, and the pen is in your hand today.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Take the one load you have been carrying toward the end and hold up your own share of it through this week — the part that is honestly yours, the whole of it, without handing any off or asking to be spelled.
cells.core:
You hold a shape under weight, and whatever you are mid-build on has kept its edges because of that. Hard week after hard week, the structure stands and you stay inside it. Comfort was not the condition.
When this is running clean, it is uneventful: one long thing near done, the same table, the same hours, everything still upright. The bend is that your attention has begun living in the next thing while this stretch still needs you. Stay with what is in your hands through the last of it. Hold up your whole share, this one share, and stop waiting to be asked whether you still can.
cells.sheetLine: You finish what you started, long after it stopped being interesting.

cells.tense: You will have to be the steady one again, and you are already braced for it.
cells.act: leave the heart open and empty a while
cells.ask: Choose one morning and give it ten empty minutes — nothing queued, no plan, nobody to be steady for — and let whatever wants to reach you find you in that quiet.
cells.core:
When people need something held, you arrive braced. The preparations are on before the ask comes: what they'll need, what you'll say, how long you can keep it up. Some of that foresight is your real gift. Lately it outruns the day it is preparing for.
What is going right is quiet — a steady hand while things burn, a promise made good, someone's bad night carried into morning. You are holding more than your half and rehearsing tomorrow's half too. Let one morning find you unprepared. Sit empty a while. Whatever shows up in that quiet is the part you don't usually get to meet, and none of it needs managing.
cells.sheetLine: You brace for tomorrow before today is even over.

cells.tense: The work was completed, and you are standing at a threshold you already crossed.
cells.act: describe what is in front of your eyes in five plain lines, no conclusions
cells.ask: Pick one ordinary thing close by — a counter, a plant, the road — and put five plain lines about it on paper, nothing added from what you know, no last line telling you what it means.
cells.core:
The long thing got finished, or nearly, and the easy story was that you were tired. Lately a small task takes a whole evening, and you have been calling that ordinary. The eye that used to catch what mattered goes soft the longer you lean on it, and rest does not bring it back.
A good stretch here is just doing the next thing — lifting a pot, finishing the report — with no announcement in your head about what it says about you. The first-look faculty has gone quiet, so everything waits for the whole frame before anything is worth beginning. It needs something to look at, not pushing. Something ordinary close by, described plainly, no verdict.
cells.sheetLine: What's near you has stopped being worth a first look.

cells.tense: The things standing in this life got built by someone, and the account you keep has you off the page.
cells.ask: Next time something you kept upright is praised, look at what actually happened before you set it aside — stay with the plain facts a moment, then answer with what you did.
cells.core:
You are the one who keeps the long things standing, and it does not occur to you to claim it. A project ends and you are surprised to be thanked, because in your version you were nearby, lending a hand. The load was yours. The story has you at the edge of the room.
When this is working, you carry weight with no announcement — the whole of what you said you'd hold, nothing made of it. Now the work is unchanged and the ownership of it has quietly drifted off you. So before you set the thanks aside, look at what actually happened and hold the plain version as true. Stay with it a moment. That alone is the correction.
cells.sheetLine: You carry the whole load and call it helping.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that a material cycle has reached its own natural completion — the record says too little may locate the person behind the present, not narrate the completion; I have narrowed it to a hand that keeps steadying and says it is just tired. The reader could reasonably say it is not tiredness but plain disuse, and the ask survives being wrong: describing a scene costs nothing and brightens the eye regardless. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'the ground doesn't need a witness' — a fine line, and I cut it.
